work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter the King, Gloucester, Bishop of Winchester, Exeter, York, Warwick and Vernon; Suffolk, Somerset, Basset and others. To them, with his soldiers, Talbot.

lines.text: My gracious Prince, and honourable peers,
lines.plainText: My gracious Prince and honourable peers

lines.text: Hearing of your arrival in this realm,
lines.plainText: Hearing of your arrival in this realm

lines.text: I have awhile given truce unto my wars
lines.plainText: I have awhile given truce unto my wars

lines.text: To do my duty to my sovereign;
lines.plainText: To do my duty to my sovereign

lines.text: In sign whereof, this arm, that hath reclaim'd
lines.plainText: In sign whereof this arm that hath reclaim'd

lines.text: To your obedience fifty fortresses,
lines.plainText: To your obedience fifty fortresses

lines.text: Twelve cities and seven walled towns of strength,
lines.plainText: Twelve cities and seven walled towns of strength

lines.text: Beside five hundred prisoners of esteem,
lines.plainText: Beside five hundred prisoners of esteem

lines.text: Lets fall his sword before your Highness' feet,
lines.plainText: Lets fall his sword before your Highness' feet

lines.text: And with submissive loyalty of heart
lines.plainText: And with submissive loyalty of heart

lines.text: Ascribes the glory of his conquest got
lines.plainText: Ascribes the glory of his conquest got

lines.text: First to my God, and next unto your Grace. [Kneels.]
lines.plainText: First to my God and next unto your Grace Kneels

lines.text: Is this the Lord Talbot, uncle Gloucester,
lines.plainText: Is this the Lord Talbot uncle Gloucester

lines.text: That hath so long been resident in France?
lines.plainText: That hath so long been resident in France

lines.text: Yes, if it please your Majesty, my liege.
lines.plainText: Yes if it please your Majesty my liege

lines.text: Welcome, brave captain and victorious lord!
lines.plainText: Welcome brave captain and victorious lord

lines.text: When I was young, as yet I am not old,
lines.plainText: When I was young as yet I am not old

lines.text: I do remember how my father said
lines.plainText: I do remember how my father said

lines.text: A stouter champion never handled sword.
lines.plainText: A stouter champion never handled sword

lines.text: Long since we were resolved of your truth,
lines.plainText: Long since we were resolved of your truth

lines.text: Your faithful service, and your toil in war;
lines.plainText: Your faithful service and your toil in war

lines.text: Yet never have you tasted our reward,
lines.plainText: Yet never have you tasted our reward

lines.text: Or been reguerdon'd with so much as thanks.
lines.plainText: Or been reguerdon'd with so much as thanks

lines.text: Because till now we never saw your face.
lines.plainText: Because till now we never saw your face

lines.text: Therefore, stand up; and for these good deserts
lines.plainText: Therefore stand up and for these good deserts

lines.text: We here create you Earl of Shrewsbury;
lines.plainText: We here create you Earl of Shrewsbury

lines.text: And in our coronation take your place.
lines.plainText: And in our coronation take your place

content.text: [Sennet. Flourish. Exeunt all but Vernon and Basset.]

lines.text: Now, sir, to you that were so hot at sea,
lines.plainText: Now sir to you that were so hot at sea

lines.text: Disgracing of these colours that I wear
lines.plainText: Disgracing of these colours that I wear

lines.text: In honour of my noble Lord of York,
lines.plainText: In honour of my noble Lord of York

lines.text: Dar'st thou maintain the former words thou spak'st?
lines.plainText: Dar'st thou maintain the former words thou spak'st

lines.text: Yes, sir, as well as you dare patronage
lines.plainText: Yes sir as well as you dare patronage

lines.text: The envious barking of your saucy tongue
lines.plainText: The envious barking of your saucy tongue

lines.text: Against my lord the Duke of Somerset.
lines.plainText: Against my lord the Duke of Somerset

lines.text: Sirrah, thy lord I honour as he is.
lines.plainText: Sirrah thy lord I honour as he is

lines.text: Why, what is he? As good a man as York.
lines.plainText: Why what is he As good a man as York

lines.text: Hark ye; not so: in witness, take ye that.
lines.plainText: Hark ye not so in witness take ye that

lines.text: Villain, thou knowest the law of arms is such
lines.plainText: Villain thou knowest the law of arms is such

lines.text: That whoso draws a sword, 'tis present death,
lines.plainText: That whoso draws a sword 'tis present death

lines.text: Or else this blow should broach thy dearest blood.
lines.plainText: Or else this blow should broach thy dearest blood

lines.text: But I'll unto his Majesty, and crave
lines.plainText: But I'll unto his Majesty and crave

lines.text: I may have liberty to venge this wrong;
lines.plainText: I may have liberty to venge this wrong

lines.text: When thou shalt see I'll meet thee to thy cost.
lines.plainText: When thou shalt see I'll meet thee to thy cost

lines.text: Well, miscreant, I'll be there as soon as you;
lines.plainText: Well miscreant I'll be there as soon as you

lines.text: And, after, meet you sooner than you would.
lines.plainText: And after meet you sooner than you would
